lessons.title: Release is a movement too
lessons.goal: Release each key without lifting the whole shoulder.
steps: Play C4 with finger 1, then D4 with 2; let the previous key rise completely.
Alternate four slow attacks with four silent wrist releases. Keep the forearm level rather than dropping below the keyboard.
Listen for separated notes, then connect C-D-E using a light transfer of weight; compare detached and connected sound.
lessons.pattern: C D E D C; one beat each, first detached then connected
quiz: What ends a detached piano note?

lessons.title: Read C, D and E
lessons.goal: Locate middle C, D and E relative to the treble staff.
steps: Find C4 on the ledger line below the treble staff; D4 is the space above it, E4 the bottom line.
Point to the three positions and say their names before touching a key.
Write C-E-D-C in letter names; play one quarter note per beat, then cover the labels and read by position.
lessons.pattern: | C4 E4 D4 C4 |; four quarter notes
quiz: Where is E4 in treble clef?

lessons.title: A step or a skip?
lessons.goal: Hear the difference between a second and a third.
steps: Play C-D slowly, sing both notes, and describe the small upward step.
Play C-E and sing again; this third skips D in the letter sequence.
Ask a helper to play either pair unseen, or use the interval challenge for seconds and thirds; check ten guesses by replaying.
lessons.pattern: C-D (second); C-E (third); listen before looking
quiz: C to E spans which interval?

lessons.title: Four beats, one bar
lessons.goal: Play four quarter notes without adding time at the bar line.
steps: Set 40 BPM and say 1-2-3-4 for two bars before playing.
Play C4 on each number; lift and re-attack gently for repeated notes.
Play bar two immediately after bar one. Then omit beat 3 but continue counting through the rest.
lessons.pattern: | C C C C | C C rest C |; each event lasts one beat
quiz: During a one-beat rest you should...

lessons.title: Original piece: Window Light
lessons.goal: Play a two-bar melody with a clear final rest.
steps: Learn bar one C-D-E-D using fingers 1-2-3-2.
Bar two is C held for two beats, then two one-beat rests; keep the fingers close while the key rises.
Join the bars twice, hear the ending in silence, and climb the tempo ladder only after two controlled takes.
quiz: How long is the final C?

lessons.title: Left-hand home position
lessons.goal: Play C3 to G3 with left-hand fingers 5 to 1.
steps: Set left little finger 5 on C3 and thumb 1 on G3; check that the wrist can move freely.
Ascend C-D-E-F-G with 5-4-3-2-1 and descend with 1-2-3-4-5.
Play hands separately, then both hands in parallel a register apart; shorten to three notes if coordination tightens.
lessons.pattern: LH C3 D3 E3 F3 G3 and back; one beat each
quiz: Left-hand finger on C3 in this position?

lessons.title: Read the bass staff
lessons.goal: Find bass-clef C3, E3 and G3.
steps: Bass lines from bottom upward are G2-B2-D3-F3-A3; spaces are A2-C3-E3-G3.
Find C3 in the second space and E3 in the third space. G3 is the top space, not the bottom line.
Play C3-E3-G3-E3 and sing its contour; draw the spaces on paper and remove letter labels on the second pass.
lessons.pattern: | C3 E3 G3 E3 |; four quarter notes

lessons.title: Major and minor five-note colours
lessons.goal: Compare C major and C minor pentachords.
steps: Play C-D-E-F-G using one finger per note, then repeat with Eb instead of E.
Keep C and G unchanged; only lower the third E to Eb for this minor five-note set.
Sing the third in each pattern and try identifying which colour a helper plays without watching.
lessons.pattern: C D E F G; C D Eb F G (displayed D#)
quiz: Which change makes this C pentachord minor?

lessons.title: Dynamic echoes
lessons.goal: Repeat the same pulse at two controlled volumes.
steps: Play C-D-E-D at a moderate volume, then repeat softly without changing tempo.
Count all eight beats; a quiet note still needs a complete key movement.
Swap roles between hands. Listen for even timing rather than treating loudness as an accent on every note.
lessons.pattern: | C D E D | C D E D |; medium then soft

lessons.title: Original piece: Morning Echo
lessons.goal: Play a right-hand phrase and left-hand answer.
steps: Right hand plays C4-E4-G4-E4 for one bar.
Left hand answers C3-D3-E3-C3 for the next bar; do not overlap the last note with the answer unless intentionally legato.
Repeat with a softer answer. Name the first interval and maintain the same pulse across the hand change.
lessons.pattern: RH | C4 E4 G4 E4 | LH | C3 D3 E3 C3 |
quiz: The left hand in a lower register

lessons.title: A tie crosses the bar
lessons.goal: Hold a tied note without striking it again.
steps: Count two bars of 4/4. Play E4 on beat 4 and hold it through beat 1 of the next bar.
A tie joins the same pitch and adds its durations; do not confuse it with a slur between different pitches.
Play C-D-rest-E tied to E-rest-D-C. Clap the attacks before playing.
quiz: A tied E across two beats is...
One attack held for both beats

lessons.title: Move the five-note home to G
lessons.goal: Play the G major pentachord without changing its interval pattern.
steps: Move the right thumb to G4 and play G-A-B-C5-D5.
Notice this five-note set uses only white keys; the complete G scale will introduce F# later.
Compare C-D-E-F-G and G-A-B-C-D by singing scale degrees 1-2-3-4-5 rather than memorising key locations.
lessons.pattern: G4 A4 B4 C5 D5 and back; fingers 1-2-3-4-5
quiz: The third of this G pentachord is...

lessons.title: Build A minor
lessons.goal: Play A-C-E and distinguish it from C major.
steps: Play A3-C4-E4 separately, then together using comfortable fingers 1-3-5.
Compare the minor third A-C with the major third C-E in C major.
Change Am to C once per four beats; keep common C and E close rather than jumping the whole hand.
lessons.pattern: | Am(4) | C(4) |; Am=A C E

lessons.title: Two notes inside a beat
lessons.goal: Place eighth notes evenly between clicks.
steps: At 40 BPM say 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &; clap each syllable evenly.
Play C-D-E-D-C-D-E-G as eighth notes in one bar.
Alternate one bar of quarters with one bar of eighths. The metronome stays at the same quarter-note tempo.
lessons.pattern: | C D E D C D E G |; eight eighth notes, count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &

lessons.title: Original piece: Paper Kite
lessons.goal: Compose a four-bar answer with a held bass root.
steps: Use RH | C D E G | A G E D | and hold LH C3 for four beats per bar.
Create two answer bars using C-D-E-G-A, ending on C4 for two beats and two beats of silence.
Write every beat and rest on paper. Practise each hand separately before performing all four bars twice.
lessons.pattern: Two given quarter-note bars; two original answer bars; LH C3(4) each bar
quiz: Account for four beats including rests

lessons.title: Together in, together out
lessons.goal: Attack and release a triad together without squeezing.
steps: Play C-E-G slowly as a chord; listen for one onset rather than three accidental staggered notes.
Hold for two beats, release for two, then repeat four times.
Play the same exercise with Am. If one note misses, test that finger separately instead of adding force.
lessons.pattern: C chord(2), rest(2); Am chord(2), rest(2)
quiz: Uneven chord notes are best fixed by...
Checking each finger and slowing down

lessons.title: F major's flat
lessons.goal: Play F-G-A-Bb-C with an accurate flat fourth.
steps: Place five fingers on F4-G4-A4-Bb4-C5; Bb is the black key just below B.
Play ascending then descending, saying the letter names and noticing the half step A-Bb.
Compare with C's five-note set by ear. The flat preserves the same major-pentachord spacing after transposition.
lessons.pattern: F G A Bb C and back; Bb appears as A# in the pitch guide
quiz: F major needs which altered note?

lessons.title: Read C, Am and F symbols
lessons.goal: Translate three chord symbols into triads.
steps: C means C-E-G; Am means A-C-E; F means F-A-C. The small m means minor.
Play each as separated tones, then use a four-beat blocked chord under its symbol.
Write | C | Am | F | C | and practise one change per bar without adding a pause.

lessons.title: A gentle three-beat sway
lessons.goal: Keep three quarter-note beats per bar.
steps: Count 1-2-3, stressing 1 lightly; a 3/4 bar contains three quarter-note beats.
Play LH C3 on 1 and RH C-E-G chord on 2 and 3; rehearse each hand separately.
Change to F then C once per bar. Do not insert a fourth beat because the app's backing has four beats; use the click and your own count.
lessons.pattern: 3/4: LH root on 1; RH chord on 2,3; C-F-C-C

lessons.title: Original piece: Lantern Song
lessons.goal: Accompany a simple melody with roots and triads.
steps: Melody quarters: | E G E C | C E A G | A G F E | D C C(2) |.
Use harmony C-Am-F-C and LH roots C3-A2-F3-C3 held once per bar; learn hands apart.
Play melody and bass together, then try the triads alone as an accompaniment version. Sing the melody over that version to hear the chords' roles.
lessons.pattern: 4/4 melody over | C | Am | F | C |; final C held two beats

lessons.title: G major and the leading tone
lessons.goal: Play G major with F# and smooth thumb crossing.
steps: RH G-A-B-C-D-E-F#-G uses 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5; descend in reverse.
Isolate E-F#-G and hear F# lead into G; compare with F natural to hear the difference.
Practise one octave at 50 BPM, then sing the eighth degree as a return to home rather than a new key.
lessons.pattern: G major: G A B C D E F# G and back

lessons.title: D major: two sharps
lessons.goal: Apply F# and C# consistently in D major.
steps: Read the two-sharp signature as F# and C# in every octave unless cancelled.
RH D-E-F#-G-A-B-C#-D uses the same 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5 pattern.
Write a two-bar D-F#-A-C# phrase and play it; finish C#-D to hear the leading tone resolve.
lessons.pattern: D E F# G A B C# D; finish C# D
quiz: Which notes are sharp in D major?

lessons.title: Thirds by ear and touch
lessons.goal: Identify major and minor thirds within C major.
steps: Play C-E, D-F and E-G; count three letter names in every pair.
Compare the four-semitone C-E major third with the three-semitone D-F minor third.
Shuffle these pairs with a helper and sing the upper note first; check by playing the lower and upper notes together.
lessons.pattern: C-E major; D-F minor; E-G minor

lessons.title: I-IV-V in D
lessons.goal: Build a D-G-A-D cadence using the key's sharps.
steps: Build D-F#-A, G-B-D and A-C#-E; say root-third-fifth for each.
Play four beats per chord with LH D3-G3-A3-D3 roots.
Reduce to two bars if changing to A loses C#; compare A major against A minor to hear why the dominant needs C#.
quiz: The V chord of D major is...

lessons.title: Original piece: Compass
lessons.goal: Transpose a short major melody from C to G and D.
steps: Use scale degrees 1-2-3-5 | 4-3-2-1, one quarter per beat.
Play it in C, then G, then D, writing each key's necessary sharps.
Keep the same fingering roles where comfortable and sing the contour; changing the home note should not change the rhythm.
lessons.pattern: In D: | D E F# A | G F# E D |; also transpose to C and G

lessons.title: A broken-chord engine
lessons.goal: Keep a low-high-middle-high accompaniment even.
steps: LH C3-G3-E3-G3 uses 5-1-3-1 where comfortable; play four quarters first.
RH holds E4 for the whole bar while LH moves. Then change RH only every two beats.
Reverse roles briefly to understand which hand supplies movement. Keep the accompaniment quieter than the held melody.
lessons.pattern: LH | C3 G3 E3 G3 |; RH E4(4) then G4(2) E4(2)

lessons.title: A natural minor
lessons.goal: Play A natural minor and relate it to C major.
steps: A-B-C-D-E-F-G-A uses the same white notes as C major but a different home.
RH one octave uses 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5; hear the half steps B-C and E-F.
Improvise a two-bar answer finishing on A, not C. Compare which ending feels settled.
lessons.pattern: A B C D E F G A; natural minor
quiz: A natural minor shares notes with...

lessons.title: Four-chord pop connection
lessons.goal: Connect C-G-Am-F with common tones.
steps: RH shapes C-E-G, B-D-G, C-E-A, C-F-A keep the register close.
LH roots C3-G2-A2-F2 change once per bar; practise the right-hand changes before adding bass.
Compare the top voice G-G-A-A with root-position jumps. Listen for continuity rather than a louder chord at each change.
lessons.pattern: | C | G | Am | F |; four beats each, close RH voicings
quiz: To change every chord to minor

lessons.title: Dotted quarter and eighth
lessons.goal: Count a dotted quarter followed by an eighth.
steps: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &; hold C from 1 through 2, play D on the & of 2.
Play E on 3 and G on 4. The first C lasts one-and-a-half beats, D half a beat.
Clap the pattern, then play against LH whole-note roots; keep the next bar's first beat in place.
quiz: One and a half quarter-note beats

lessons.title: Original piece: City Lights
lessons.goal: Play a four-chord melody with a moving accompaniment.
steps: LH broken chords use root-fifth-third-fifth for C, G, Am and F, one note per quarter beat.
Join two bars at a time; on a final take simplify LH to roots if necessary, then restore the pattern without rushing.
lessons.pattern: RH half-note melody over C-G-Am-F; LH four-quarter broken chords
quiz: Steady and quieter than the melody

lessons.title: Slurs and staccato
lessons.goal: Differentiate phrase legato from detached articulation.
steps: A slur groups different pitches into a connected phrase; a tie connects identical pitches into one duration.
Play C-D-E-F connected, then G-E-D-C lightly detached; do not use pedal to hide gaps.
Write a slur over the first bar and dots over the second on paper; listen to the contrast with identical quarter-note timing.
lessons.pattern: | C D E F | G E D C |; first bar slurred, second staccato
quiz: A slur between C and D means...
Connect different pitches in a phrase

lessons.title: F major thumb placement
lessons.goal: Play F major without crossing onto Bb awkwardly.
steps: Isolate Bb-C so the thumb lands on white C, not the black Bb.
Descend with 4-3-2-1-4-3-2-1; practise slowly and write the flat signature at the start of your note list.
lessons.pattern: RH F G A Bb C D E F; 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4
quiz: RH thumb crossing in F major happens after...

lessons.title: Cadence and phrase breathing
lessons.goal: Hear a half cadence and a return-home cadence.
steps: Play C-F-G and stop; sing the final G harmony and notice the unfinished quality.
Repeat C-F-G-C and listen to the settled ending.
Play the melody E-F-D-C over the second sequence, relaxing the final C rather than clipping it. Leave a measured rest between phrases.
lessons.pattern: First phrase ends G; second phrase resolves G-C; melody E F D C
quiz: A phrase ending on V often feels...

lessons.title: Two big beats in 6/8
lessons.goal: Feel six eighth notes grouped into two beats.
steps: Count 1-la-li 2-la-li at a slow comfortable pulse; clap six equal subdivisions.
Play C-E-G on the first group and D-F-G on the second.
Keep accents on subdivision 1 and 4, not three equal pairs. Use the metronome for the dotted-quarter groups and avoid the four-beat backing.
lessons.pattern: 6/8: | C E G D F G |; two groups of three eighths

lessons.title: Original piece: Small Minuet
lessons.goal: Shape a four-bar 3/4 dance phrase.
steps: LH plays C3 then G2 then F2 then C3, held three beats each; no four-beat backing.
Build toward bar two and soften the final bar. Perform once detached and once legato, then choose the phrasing you prefer.

lessons.title: A dominant seventh colour
lessons.goal: Build C7, F7 and G7 with a minor seventh.
steps: C7 adds Bb to C-E-G; F7 adds Eb to F-A-C; G7 adds F to G-B-D.
Play root-third-seventh slowly; then add the fifth only if your hand remains comfortable.
Compare C major with C7 by singing Bb resolving to A over F. Work chord tones separately before the blocked shape.
lessons.pattern: C7=C E G Bb; F7=F A C Eb; G7=G B D F

lessons.title: C minor blues vocabulary
lessons.goal: Play C-Eb-F-Gb-G-Bb-C accurately.
steps: Name six distinct scale tones C-Eb-F-Gb-G-Bb before returning to C.
Break into C-Eb-F and Gb-G-Bb-C fragments; the Gb is a passing colour, not a note to lean on indefinitely.
Over a C root, make a short phrase ending on C or G; sing it before playing and include silence.
lessons.pattern: C Eb F Gb G Bb C (flats displayed as sharps)
quiz: The blues passing tone between F and G is...

lessons.title: Swing without guessing
lessons.goal: Place long-short eighth-note pairs over a steady beat.
steps: At 50 BPM count triplet subdivisions 1-trip-let; play on 1 and let, leaving trip silent.
Repeat C-C pairs, then C-Eb, maintaining the quarter-note click.
Compare one straight-eighth bar with one swing bar. This is a triplet practice model; real swing ratio changes with tempo and style.
lessons.pattern: Four long-short pairs per bar; first two and final triplet subdivisions
quiz: In the triplet swing model, attacks fall on...

lessons.title: Read a twelve-bar blues map
lessons.goal: Follow a twelve-bar C blues form without losing place.
steps: Play LH roots for four beats per bar while saying each bar number aloud.
Add RH third and seventh on beat 1. If lost, simplify to roots and rejoin at bar 1; the app's C-F-G-C backing is not this twelve-bar form.
lessons.pattern: 12 bars: C7 C7 C7 C7 F7 F7 C7 C7 G7 F7 C7 C7

lessons.title: Original piece: Porch Blues
lessons.goal: Create a repeat-and-answer motif over twelve bars.
steps: Use | C(1) Eb(1) F(1) G(1) | then | Bb(2) G(1) C(1) | as your two-bar idea.
Repeat the idea in bars 1-4, vary its ending over F7 in bars 5-6, and leave space in bars 7-8.
Answer in bars 9-12 with the blues scale and resolve to C. LH roots mark the form; write one variation before trying it.
lessons.pattern: Two-bar motif over the printed twelve-bar C blues form
quiz: A useful blues motif can be developed by...
Repeating it then changing its ending

lessons.title: Major seven, minor seven, dominant
lessons.goal: Distinguish Cmaj7, Dm7 and G7 by chord tones.
steps: Play C-E-G-B for Cmaj7, D-F-A-C for Dm7 and G-B-D-F for G7.
Compare major seventh B and minor seventh Bb over C; name the symbol before sounding it.
Use LH roots plus RH third/seventh pairs to avoid wide stretches. Listen for the different seventh colours, not just the roots.
lessons.pattern: Cmaj7; Dm7; G7; separate tones then safe blocked voicings
quiz: Cmaj7 differs from C7 because it has...

lessons.title: ii-V-I guide tones
lessons.goal: Connect Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 with small voice movements.
steps: LH roots D3-G2-C3; RH pairs F4-C5, F4-B4, E4-B4.
Hold common F through the first change and common B through the second; listen to C descending to B then F to E.
Play one four-beat bar per chord plus a second Cmaj7 bar. Change hand positions silently before adding rhythm.
lessons.pattern: | Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 | Cmaj7 |; guide tones F-C, F-B, E-B
quiz: In G7 resolving to Cmaj7, F usually moves to...

lessons.title: Choose a scale from the chord
lessons.goal: Use chord tones as phrase anchors in a C-major ii-V-I.
steps: All three chords Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 can use the C-major note collection in this exercise.
Start Dm7 on F or A, G7 on B or F, and Cmaj7 on E or B to make harmony audible.
Play one anchor on beat 1 then two nearby passing notes. Naming a mode is less important than hearing its chord-tone resolution.
lessons.pattern: Dm7 F-G-A; G7 B-A-F; Cmaj7 E-D-C
quiz: A strong G7 guide tone is...

lessons.title: A lead sheet is a set of choices
lessons.goal: Read melody rhythm and chord symbols as separate layers.
steps: Write melody | F(2) A(2) | B(1) A(1) F(2) | E(2) D(1) C(1) | C(4) | above Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7.
Play melody alone, then comp chord shells alone on beats 1 and 3.
Join with roots only first. A chord symbol supplies harmony, not a prescribed finger or rhythm; choose a sparse accompaniment.
lessons.pattern: 4-bar ii-V-I lead sheet; melody durations above, sparse comp on 1 and 3
quiz: Harmony to realise with a chosen voicing

lessons.title: Original piece: Corner Cafe
lessons.goal: Perform and vary a ii-V-I melody with clear guide tones.
steps: Play the lead-sheet melody from the previous lesson twice over Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7.
Second time change just the rhythm of the first two notes while keeping four beats in each bar.
Keep the melody louder than shells and leave the last bar simple. Judge harmonic clarity and phrasing by listening, not the pitch detector.
lessons.pattern: Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 | Cmaj7; original four-bar melody and one variation
quiz: For a controlled first variation, change...
One feature while retaining the form
All notes, rhythms and chords at once

lessons.title: Bring out the top voice
lessons.goal: Balance a melody above quieter chord tones.
steps: RH C4-E4-G4 chord: listen for G4 as the melodic voice, with C and E softer.
Practise G alone, then add light C and E without pressing the whole hand equally.
Move to C-F-A and B-D-G with the same top-voice intention. Rest after each short repetition and avoid stretching for force.
lessons.pattern: C-E-G -> C-F-A -> B-D-G; highlight top notes G-A-G
quiz: Giving different musical lines different prominence

lessons.title: A harmonic minor and its pull
lessons.goal: Play A harmonic minor with G# leading to A.
steps: A-B-C-D-E-F-G#-A raises only G from natural minor.
Sing F-G#-A slowly and notice the wide augmented second F-G#.
Build E-G#-B and resolve it to A-C-E. Keep the raised seventh consistent when improvising a short minor cadence.
lessons.pattern: A B C D E F G# A; E major -> A minor

lessons.title: Accidentals and cancellation
lessons.goal: Apply and cancel a written accidental within a bar.
steps: Write | G# A G# E | then | G A B A | in A natural minor.
The explicit G# applies to that staff position through the first bar; the new bar returns to the key signature unless marked otherwise.
Write a natural sign before a second G in the first bar and play the changed version. Say the actual pitches before touching keys.
lessons.pattern: | G# A G# E | G natural A B A |; four quarters per bar
quiz: After the bar line, an isolated accidental normally...

lessons.title: Expressive timing with a return
lessons.goal: Shape a phrase without losing its underlying pulse.
steps: First play | A(1) C(1) E(2) | D(1) B(1) A(2) | strictly against the click.
In a solo version lengthen the high E slightly, then recover time gently through the descent without inserting a new beat.
Return to strict time on the next phrase; if playing with others, agree on the breathing point instead of imposing free timing.
lessons.pattern: Two 4/4 bars; strict baseline, small rubato at E, return at next phrase
quiz: Keep phrase direction and recover the agreed pulse

lessons.title: Original piece: Evening Study
lessons.goal: Combine minor cadence, balance and clean pedal.
steps: RH | A C E C | G# B E B | A(2) C(1) B(1) | A(4) | over LH A2-E3-A2-A2.
Learn without pedal first, keeping the top line audible above any added inner tones.
Add pedal only at harmony changes and lift at the final release; or demonstrate finger legato if no pedal is available. Give two uninterrupted takes with a planned soft ending.
lessons.pattern: 4/4 in A minor; harmony Am-E-Am-Am; final A whole note
quiz: The E-major chord in A minor needs...

lessons.title: Carry an offbeat over beat one
lessons.goal: Hold a syncopated note across a bar line.
steps: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & and attack E4 only on the & after 4.
Tie E through beat 1 of the next bar, release on 2, then play G on 3 and C on 4.
LH plays C3 on each numbered beat in a separate pass, then combine; avoid re-attacking the tied RH note when LH reaches 1.
lessons.pattern: RH E on 4& tied through next beat 1; rest beat 2; G on 3, C on 4
quiz: At the new bar's beat 1, the tied RH should...
Remain held without a new attack

lessons.title: Pentatonic in three keys
lessons.goal: Transpose major pentatonic vocabulary to G and F.
steps: C major pentatonic is C-D-E-G-A; G is G-A-B-D-E; F is F-G-A-C-D.
Play each in a comfortable register, then sing the degrees 1-2-3-5-6.
Move a two-beat C-D-E idea to each key. Keep its rhythm unchanged and aim for the new root on the last beat.
lessons.pattern: G A B D E; F G A C D; transpose degrees 1-2-3

lessons.title: Three against two, slowly
lessons.goal: Coordinate a basic three-against-two rhythm.
steps: Count six equal subdivisions; RH attacks on 1,3,5 and LH on 1,4.
Tap on the lid first, then use RH C4 and LH C3 for one cycle; both hands start together on 1.
Repeat four cycles at a slow shared pulse. This is a coordination drill, not a reason to turn the metronome into six unrelated beats.
lessons.pattern: Six slots: RH x . x . x . ; LH x . . x . .
quiz: The hands coincide on which subdivision?

lessons.title: Sparse offbeat comping
lessons.goal: Comp a pop progression without covering the melody.
steps: Use C-E-G, B-D-G, C-E-A, C-F-A voicings over C-G-Am-F.
Play RH on beat 1 and the & after 3 only; LH roots stay on beats 1 and 3.
Sing a short melody over the groove. Remove a chord attack if the sung line becomes crowded; judge space as well as harmonic accuracy.
lessons.pattern: C-G-Am-F; RH attacks 1 and 3&; LH roots 1,3
quiz: Changing every chord to a scale

lessons.title: Original piece: Night Bus
lessons.goal: Maintain an offbeat melody over stable bass changes.
steps: Answer with | rest(0.5) E(0.5) A(1) G(2) | F(1) E(1) C(2) |.
LH roots mark C-G-Am-F once per bar. Clap RH alone before adding LH; do not claim a faster ladder target if the first offbeat keeps moving.
lessons.pattern: Four bars over C-G-Am-F; first three begin on 1&; final C two beats
quiz: The first melody attack is on...

lessons.title: Sequence, answer, contrast
lessons.goal: Develop one motif in three recognisable ways.
steps: Start C-D-E-rest as four quarter-note events; repeat it exactly once.
Sequence it from F as F-G-A-rest, then answer E-D-C-rest.
Create a contrasting held-note phrase while retaining the four-beat bar. Write the three variants so improvisation becomes a deliberate choice.
lessons.pattern: C D E rest; F G A rest; E D C rest; then a contrasting held note
quiz: Starting pitch while preserving a recognisable pattern

lessons.title: Dorian versus natural minor
lessons.goal: Hear D Dorian's raised sixth compared with D natural minor.
steps: D Dorian uses D-E-F-G-A-B-C-D; D natural minor substitutes Bb for B.
Play both slowly, sing A-B-C versus A-Bb-C, and hear the sixth's colour.
Over Dm7, use D-F-A-C as anchors and B as a passing colour. Do not replace chord-tone listening with running the entire scale.
lessons.pattern: D Dorian D E F G A B C D; compare Bb in natural minor

lessons.title: Plan an A-A-B-A form
lessons.goal: Read a sixteen-bar arrangement roadmap.
steps: Define A as four bars C-Am-F-G; define B as four bars Dm-G-C-C.
Write A-A-B-A, then number all sixteen bars so repeated sections do not hide the form.
Play roots only while naming bar and section. Add melody only after you can move from the bridge back to A on time.
lessons.pattern: 16 bars: A(C Am F G), A, B(Dm G C C), A
quiz: How long is this A-A-B-A form?

lessons.title: Choose texture and register
lessons.goal: Use three accompaniment textures without obscuring the melody.
steps: Play the same C-Am-F-G cycle with LH whole-note roots, then broken chords, then sparse RH chord shells.
Choose one texture for A and a contrasting one for B; keep the melody above the accompaniment register.
Listen for muddy low triads and move inner harmony upward if needed. On the last cycle simplify the ending instead of filling every beat.
lessons.pattern: C-Am-F-G; root-only, broken-chord, sparse-shell textures
quiz: A muddy low-register chord is often improved by...
Spacing voices or moving inner tones higher

lessons.title: Original piece: Open Sky
lessons.goal: Perform a sixteen-bar personal arrangement with a clear form.
steps: Use A melody | E G A G | E C A(2) | F A G F | D B G(2) | over C-Am-F-G; B melody | F A C5 A | B D5 C5 B | E G E D | C(4) | over Dm-G-C-C.
Perform A-A-B-A, varying the second A rhythm and improvising the final A with chord-tone endings.
Plan two dynamic levels and an ending, write the roadmap, then play two complete takes. Assess form, harmony, pulse and expressive intent separately.
lessons.pattern: 16-bar A-A-B-A; original melody, varied repeat, bridge, improvised return
quiz: Recognisable form, pulse and intentional musical choices
